reviewer: Claude Code (AI assistant). Not an independent human review.
method: Single printed items split from the automatic families of 1780, and of 1779 where they reach the 1780 pages (long-running ones included), counts of every item in 3 or more papers by its own opening over all 1,406 pages of 1780 in both transcriptions, a sweep of word-for-word passages shared by 4 or more papers for short items the families miss, reading of every item that meets the bar, and scan checks of each admitted and chosen passage, by the thin-year rule as amended (register Y-THIN, B1: more than half of the papers that survive for the item's weeks, and at least 4, make an item eligible; items printed by every paper in print are admitted, the others chosen to cover the months and the kinds of news)
scan_scope: Each crop covers the excerpt, the opening of the printed item. Long documents were not proofread in full.

dispositions_summary.method: The automatic families first printed in 1780 that reach 3 or more papers, long-running ones included, were split into single printed items (story_items.py --long-running, items.json: 513 items printed somewhere), and the families of 1779 were looked for on the 1780 pages (items_from_1779.json: 72 items). Every item in 3 or more papers was counted by its own opening over all 1,406 pages in both transcriptions and merged into text units (174 met the bar); every page was swept for seven-word sequences shared by 4 or more papers (87 passages no item covers, read; 13 items added); every unit that meets the bar was read, and the chosen items' openings were searched over all pages.
dispositions_summary.selection_rule: The thin-year rule (register Y-THIN) as amended by the owner's choice B1 on 23 November 2026: an item, counted by its own words, is eligible when it was printed by more than half of the newspapers that survive for its weeks, and by at least 4; digests are not. As in R-01, items printed by every newspaper that survives for their weeks are admitted, and the other eligible items are chosen to cover the months and the kinds of news, about as many stories as a standard year (about 20 to 35, a target, not a quota); one affair's items as in X-1800-01. The eligible items not chosen are listed with their counts and are not checked against the scans. Sub-stories (C-01), private persons (R-04) and the list of items read and not admitted (R-03) apply as in every year.
dispositions_summary.paper_counting: 1780 has 7 catalogue series, which are 7 papers: the Pennsylvania Packet, the New-Jersey Gazette, the New-York Gazette (New York, under the British), the Connecticut Courant, the Virginia Gazette, the New-Hampshire Gazette and the Royal South-Carolina Gazette (one issue, Charleston, 20 June). The release's map lists no misfiled RevX page for 1780; no 1780 issue has a corrected date.

counted_item_by_item.Paper counts: Every finder item of 1780 in 3 or more papers (and of 1779 over the 1780 pages) was counted by its own opening over all 1,406 pages in both transcriptions and merged into text units: 174 units met the bar. Reading them, with the sweep's passages, gave 186 items, 154 eligible; the sweep checked again on 24 November (its coverage test had been too loose) added 38 eligible items, 192 in all. Five are printed by every paper that survives for their weeks and are admitted; 23 are chosen (23 stories, 28 groups, 142 printings); 160 eligible items are listed as not chosen, 4 more that turn on private persons are listed for the owner, and 32 items read are below the bar.
counted_item_by_item.The bar: Y-THIN: more than half of the papers that survive for the item's weeks (a surviving issue between its first and last printing, and at least in the three weeks from its first printing), and at least 4. 1780 has 7 papers; 6 are in print in most weeks and 7 in the weeks of 20 June, when the Royal South-Carolina Gazette's one surviving issue counts; the bar is 4.
counted_item_by_item.Letters printed together: A letter and the papers it sends are one item (X-1810-01): General Washington's letter of 18 January with Lord Stirling's report; General Lincoln's letter of 24 May with the capitulation papers (the Virginia Gazette and the New-Hampshire Gazette print the papers without it, or later); Governor Jefferson's letter of 15 October with the dispatches it encloses (the Virginia Gazette prints the dispatches without it).
counted_item_by_item.Printed forms counted together: C-02: General Washington's general orders of 20 July under two introductions (a Chatham extract and an officer's letter of 22 July).
counted_item_by_item.Pages that recite or quote an item, or p: Not counted (C-07): Pennsylvania's bill (25 March, 6 June) and New Jersey's act (12 July) that recite Congress's resolutions of 18 March; a letter to the printer of the New-Hampshire Gazette (8 April) quoting the King's speech. Not counted (C-06): the New-Hampshire Gazette's printing of only the later part of the letter from near Morristown of 9 June.
counted_item_by_item.Judgement calls of the reading: Among the items not chosen: Congress's resolutions on Virginia's land office and on peace with the Indian nations reach the bar with two papers printing them in the journal of Congress and two quoting them in news paragraphs; the Viper's return reaches it only with two Boston wordings counted together (C-02); the Dublin paragraph on the Irish Commons stays at 3 papers (a London rewording in the New-York Gazette is not counted); one-sentence London paragraphs are items (C-09); the summons to General Lincoln, printed alone in May, is kept apart from the capitulation papers that reprint it in June; General Gates's publication of September is three items.
